title: Explicit Noetherian coefficient scheme model of a finite affine presentation
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with a specified finite presentation $\phi:A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}B$, where $r,m\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $A_0\subseteq A$ be the subring generated by the image of $\mathbf Z$ and all coefficients of the $F_j$. Write $F_{j,0}\in A_0[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ for the same polynomial with its coefficients regarded as elements of $A_0$, and set $B_0=A_0[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(F_{1,0},\ldots,F_{m,0})$. The ring $A_0$ is finitely generated over $\mathbf Z$ and is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $B_0$ is finitely presented over $A_0$. The canonical map
$$\beta:B_0\otimes_{A_0}A\longrightarrow B,\qquad b_0\otimes a\longmapsto a\,\phi(b_0)$$
is an $A$-algebra isomorphism; here $\phi(b_0)$ means the map induced by coefficient inclusion followed by the supplied presentation isomorphism. Put $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ and $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $Y_0$ admits the one-affine cover $\{Y_0\}$ by the spectrum of the Noetherian ring $A_0$. The square with vertices $\operatorname{Spec}B,X_0,\operatorname{Spec}A,Y_0$ and arrows induced by the displayed ring maps is Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, the fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ as a scheme over its residue field [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field]. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $A$ or $B$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-presentation-noetherian-coefficient-model] with $n=r$, $t_i=x_i$ and $\alpha=\phi$. Its smallest coefficient subring is exactly the specified $A_0$, and uniqueness of coefficient lifts identifies its $F_j^0$ with $F_{j,0}$, hence its quotient with the specified $B_0$. It gives finite generation of $A_0$ over $\mathbf Z$, Noetherianity of $A_0$, finite presentation of $B_0$ over $A_0$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism. For $b_0=[P]$, its formula is $[P]\otimes a\mapsto aP(\phi([x_1]),\ldots,\phi([x_r]))=a\phi(b_0)$, so that isomorphism is precisely $\beta$. No flatness is required.

source.place: Tag 055B (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-constructible), first proof paragraph: explicit affine coefficient-model reduction; algebraic construction also used in Tag 0579.

proof.text: The classes of $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ generate $B_0$ as an $A_0$-algebra: every quotient class has a polynomial representative. Thus $A_0\to B_0$ is of finite type by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For every point of $X_0$, take the entire affine opens $X_0$ and $Y_0$ in [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion]; their coordinate map is $A_0\to B_0$, so $f_0$ is locally of finite type. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and therefore quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. These two properties give finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Finally $\{Y_0\}$ covers $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ and $A_0$ is Noetherian by step 1, proving the asserted cover.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with base ring $A_0$ and algebras $B_0,A$. It identifies $X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B_0\otimes_{A_0}A)$, with projections induced by $b_0\mapsto b_0\otimes1$ and $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the ring isomorphism $\beta$ of step 1 induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}(B_0\otimes_{A_0}A)$. Its composites with the two projections are the required maps: $\beta(b_0\otimes1)=\phi(b_0)$ and $\beta(1\otimes a)=a\cdot1_B$. Thus the square formed by the specified ring maps is the fibre-product square, including both projections.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ and put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k$, formed along the canonical morphism $j_{\mathfrak p}:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification], after the ring isomorphism $e$ of $k$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ given there, $j_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{Spec}$ of the ring map $A\to k$ (germ followed by residue map); $k$ is an $A$-algebra through this map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with base ring $A$ and algebras $B,k$. This identifies the fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A k)$, and its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is induced by $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. Hence the identification is over the residue field, as asserted. The affine tensor formula has no flatness or Noetherian hypotheses; if $A=0$ there is no prime to check, and a zero fibre tensor gives the empty fibre.
